subject: history
title: Steam, Factories & Machines Adventure
welcome_lead: Britain becomes the first country to industrialise. Meet James Watt, the steam engine and the new factory world. ⚙️
meta_desc: Industrial Revolution Adventure — a KS3 History walkthrough of factories, steam power and the Industrial Revolution.
final_note: You met the steam engine and the factory system, and saw how Britain changed between 1750 and 1900.

walkthroughs.body_html:
In 1750 most British people lived in villages. They worked on farms or made cloth at home by hand.

Travel was slow — by horse, on foot, or by boat on rivers and canals. Most things were made one at a time by skilled craftsmen.

Then, between about 1750 and 1900, everything changed. We call this the Industrial Revolution.

The key new technology was the steam engine. Coal was burned to boil water; the steam pushed a piston to power machines.

Thomas Newcomen built an early version in 1712. In the 1760s and 1770s, the Scottish engineer James Watt made a much better one.

Steam could power pumps in mines, machines in factories, trains and ships. Britain had lots of coal and iron — perfect for the new age. 🔥

Instead of working at home, people now went to factories — big buildings full of machines.

In Lancashire, cotton mills spun thread on machines like the spinning jenny and water frame. Workers had to follow strict times and rules.

Towns like Manchester, Birmingham and Leeds grew very fast — this is called urbanisation. 🏭

mcqs.q: What caused the First World War?
options: Long-term tensions (militarism, alliances, imperialism, nationalism) combined with the July Crisis triggered by the assassination of Franz Ferdinand.
Germany declared war on Britain to seize colonies.
The plot aimed to make England independent from the Pope.
The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand caused the war.

mcqs.q: Why did the Schlieffen Plan fail in 1914?
options: The Schlieffen Plan failed because Britain entered the war.
Germany declared war on Britain to seize colonies.
Belgian resistance delayed the German advance; Russia mobilised faster than expected; Moltke weakened the right wing; and the French rallied at the Marne.
The Schlieffen Plan failed because it tried to invade Russia first.

mcqs.q: Why did the Gunpowder Plotters try to blow up Parliament in 1605?
options: Catholic gentlemen, frustrated that James I had not eased anti-Catholic laws as hoped, planned to kill the king and Lords and put a Catholic monarch on the throne.
The plot aimed to make England independent from the Pope.
Guy Fawkes planned and led the Gunpowder Plot.
Germany declared war on Britain to seize colonies.
